h: Walk in from Helmsley and make a day of it
p: Here's a cracking way to arrive: on foot. The Cleveland Way, one of England's National Trails, starts in Helmsley, and its first stretch takes you through woods and fields to Rievaulx in around three miles. Walk there, explore the ruins and have a bite in the café, then stroll back for tea in town. You'll earn every bit of it.
Give yourself two to three hours at the abbey. The ruins are big, the museum is worth a proper look and there's a lot of ground to cover.

Helmsley is a pretty market town with a cobbled square, independent shops, cafés and pubs. Its own castle, also cared for by English Heritage, has dramatic ruined walls and deep earthwork ditches that are fun for kids to explore. Helmsley Walled Garden, tucked below the castle, is a peaceful spot full of flowers and produce.

If you've got a car and more time, the area is stacked with gems. Byland Abbey, another Cistercian ruin, is close by, and Nunnington Hall, a National Trust house beside the River Rye, makes a lovely afternoon. Sutton Bank, on the edge of the North York Moors, has a viewpoint with huge views across the Vale of York, along with trails for walkers and cyclists. Visit Rievaulx early or late in the day and the low light on the arches is magical, perfect for photographers, before you head off to explore the rest of this beautiful corner of Yorkshire.
